title: Principles of design
examples: How do I make my artwork look balanced?
What is the difference between rhythm and pattern?
Can you show me an example of good contrast in art?

explain.say: Today we will look at principles of design. These are rules for making art look good. We will learn about balance first.
Balance means arranging things so they feel stable. Symmetrical balance looks the same on both sides. Think of a butterfly's wings.
Asymmetrical balance uses different things to look equal. A small object can balance a large one if it is colourful. This is more interesting.
Contrast is using opposites to make things stand out. You can use light next to dark, or big next to small. This makes the art pop.
Emphasis is creating a focal point in your artwork. You want the viewer's eye to go somewhere first. This is your main subject.
Rhythm is created by repeating elements. Repeating shapes or colours guides the eye across the piece. Think of waves on the beach.

faq.q: What is the difference between balance and unity?
faq.a: Balance is about making things feel steady. Unity is about making all the parts feel like they belong together as one whole.
asks: How do I make my art feel complete?
Is unity the same as harmony?

faq.q: Can I use contrast to create rhythm?
faq.a: Yes, you can. Repeating a strong contrast, like black next to white, creates a very noticeable visual rhythm.
asks: Can I use contrast in a pattern?

faq.q: Which principle is most important for a portrait?
faq.a: Emphasis is very important for a portrait. You usually want the viewer to focus on the person's face.
asks: Should I focus on balance for people?
What should I emphasize in a face?

faq.q: Is there a rule for how much contrast I can use?
faq.a: There is no strict rule. You should use contrast where you need the viewer to notice something specific.

faq.q: What is the difference between symmetry and balance?
faq.a: Symmetry is a specific type of balance where both sides are exact mirror images. Balance is the general feeling of visual stability.
asks: What is the technical term for mirror images?

facts: Balance can be symmetrical or asymmetrical.
Contrast is achieved by placing opposites near each other.
Emphasis directs the viewer's eye to a main subject.
Rhythm is created through the repetition of elements.

quiz.say: A design uses many repeating leaf shapes to guide the eye across the surface. Which principle is most evident?
quiz.why: Rhythm is created by the repetition of elements, which guides the viewer's eye across the artwork.

wrong.0: Contrast uses opposites, but this question describes repetition.
wrong.1: Emphasis points to one thing, while rhythm moves the eye across many things.
wrong.3: Balance is about stability, not the movement created by repetition.

quiz.say: An artist places a very small, bright red dot next to a huge, dull grey area. What principle is used?
quiz.show: Small dot next to large area.
quiz.why: Placing opposites like bright colour next to dull colour creates strong visual contrast.

wrong.1: This setup is about opposition, not about making the sides weigh equally.
wrong.2: While it creates emphasis, the primary technique used is the opposition of values.
wrong.3: Unity is about everything fitting together, not highlighting differences.

quiz.say: A formal portrait is designed so the left side perfectly mirrors the right side. Which principle is used?
quiz.why: Symmetrical balance means one side is a mirror image of the other side, creating formal balance.

wrong.0: Contrast deals with opposites, not the mirroring of elements.
wrong.2: This option describes an uneven but stable arrangement, not a perfect mirror.
wrong.3: Emphasis focuses on one area, but this question describes the overall structure.
